why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 4 and 5 stay close to the words. Check 6 does not. Its expect line only says "The change is one PR … whose body says Closes …". The PASS condition instead requires "exactly one PR … is open for this change", and the command uses `--state open`. Nothing in the words requires the PR to be open, so a merged or closed PR would wrongly FAIL. That is a stricter test, and it sits in a PASS/FAIL condition rather than under Advisory. Check 3(c) also requires "exits 2 with a message on stderr" for the no-argument case. The issue's "(error on stderr…)" follows "can't be read", so it most likely applies only to unreadable files. Requiring a stderr message for no arguments probably goes beyond the words too. Because of these extra requirements, the criterion fails.
